Secure Properties at a Fraction of the Cost – York County, Pennsylvania Tax Deed Sale

Discover incredible savings with York County, Pennsylvania’s annual tax sales, where you can buy properties for much less than their market value. This guide will walk you through the process, covering upset and judicial sales and showing you how to get started. Whether you’re a seasoned investor or just starting, these sales offer great opportunities for high returns and low entry costs.

Understanding the Sales

  • Upset Sale: Usually held in September, this auction starts with a bid covering delinquent taxes, current taxes, municipal liens, and costs. Properties are sold as-is, with existing liens and judgments. Bidders must register online between late August and early September.
  • Judicial Sale: If properties aren’t sold at the Upset Sale, they move to the Judicial Sale in June. These properties are offered free and clear of liens. Online registration is required in May.

Registration and Bidding

  • Registration: All bidders must register online through GovEase during specified periods before each sale. A valid photo ID is required, and no in-person registrations are accepted.
  • Deposit: Bidders must submit a 10% deposit of the final bid via wire transfer or ACH at least five days before the sale.

Additional Opportunities

  • Repository List: The Repository lists unsold properties from either sale, allowing bids anytime. Bids are subject to approval by local authorities, and the process can take up to six months.

Important Considerations

  • Due Diligence: The county sells properties without warranty. It’s essential to research thoroughly and consult an attorney before bidding.
  • Payment: Buyers must make full payment at the time of sale using certified funds. They do not accept cash.

  1. Early Registration: Register early on GovEase to ensure participation.
  2. Thorough Research: Investigate each property thoroughly. Upset sales include properties with existing liens, while judicial sales offer properties free of encumbrances.

FAQs

What is a tax lien certificate?

A tax lien certificate is a claim against a property for unpaid property taxes. Investors pay the taxes and receive a certificate that earns interest until the owner redeems it.

What is a tax deed?

A tax deed grants ownership of a property sold at a tax deed sale, usually free of prior liens and encumbrances.

How do I participate in York County’s tax sales?

Register online at GovEase during the specified registration period. Make sure to complete all required documentation.

What risks are involved?

Investing in tax liens and deeds involves risks such as property condition and existing liens. We recommend conducting thorough research and seeking legal advice.

Can I inspect the properties before bidding?

Sellers typically offer properties as-is without allowing inspections. It’s crucial to do as much research as possible.
